findings.summary: nlohmann_jsonTargets.cmake is never generated; the generated nlohmann_jsonConfig.cmake unconditionally includes it, making find_package() non-functional
findings.evidence: CMake generates nlohmann_jsonTargets.cmake via export(TARGETS nlohmann_json NAMESPACE nlohmann_json:: FILE ${NLOHMANN_JSON_CMAKE_PROJECT_TARGETS_FILE}) (CMakeLists.txt:190-194) and installs it via install(EXPORT nlohmann_jsonTargets ...) (CMakeLists.txt:200-204). The Bazel write_file target gen_nlohmann_jsonConfig_cmake (BUILD.bazel:76-103) emits content that calls include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/nlohmann_jsonTargets.cmake") at lines 84-85 of the generated file, but there is no write_file or genrule anywhere in the BUILD that produces nlohmann_jsonTargets.cmake. Any consumer that uses the generated nlohmann_jsonConfig.cmake via find_package() will hit a fatal include() error.

findings.summary: No install rules exist despite JSON_Install=ON being baked; rules_pkg is declared but never used
findings.evidence: CMake installs: header directory to CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR, Config/ConfigVersion cmake files to DATADIR/cmake/nlohmann_json, nlohmann_json.pc to DATADIR/pkgconfig, and the Targets export to the same cmake dir (CMakeLists.txt:175-209). In the Bazel BUILD the three write_file targets (gen_nlohmann_json_pc, gen_nlohmann_jsonConfigVersion_cmake, gen_nlohmann_jsonConfig_cmake) are all visibility=['//visibility:private'] and are never referenced by any pkg_install, pkg_filegroup, or pkg_files rule. rules_pkg 1.0.1 is declared in MODULE.bazel:4 but no load() or rule from it appears anywhere in elements/nlohmann-json/BUILD.bazel. The include/ header tree is also never wired to an install destination. The generated artifacts are compile-time dead ends.

findings.summary: C++11 minimum standard requirement is not propagated to consumers of the cc_library
findings.evidence: CMake applies target_compile_features(nlohmann_json INTERFACE cxx_std_11) (CMakeLists.txt:108), which forces any target linking nlohmann_json to compile as at least C++11. The Bazel cc_library target (BUILD.bazel:105-156) has no copts, features, or toolchain constraint enforcing cxx_std_11. Downstream Bazel targets that link :nlohmann_json and compile as C++98 or C++03 will silently succeed at configuration time and only fail (or produce silent miscompiles) at compile time.

findings.summary: Single-include (amalgamated) variant has no Bazel representation; JSON_MultipleHeaders=OFF path is entirely absent
findings.evidence: CMake supports JSON_MultipleHeaders=OFF which switches NLOHMANN_JSON_INCLUDE_BUILD_DIR to single_include/ (CMakeLists.txt:75-77) and the library target then exposes single_include/nlohmann/json.hpp and single_include/nlohmann/json_fwd.hpp instead of the multi-header tree. CI explicitly tests this path via ci_test_single_header (ci.cmake:619-627). The Bazel BUILD has exactly one cc_library listing only the multi-header include/ tree (BUILD.bazel:105-156); single_include/ appears nowhere and there is no select() or second cc_library target to express this alternative.

findings.summary: MSVC natvis debug-view file is not represented: neither added as an interface source nor wired to an install rule
findings.evidence: CMake conditionally adds nlohmann_json.natvis as a target_sources(INTERFACE ...) entry when MSVC is detected (CMakeLists.txt:129-138) and installs it to the install prefix root via install(FILES ${NLOHMANN_NATVIS_FILE} DESTINATION .) (CMakeLists.txt:185-188). The Bazel cc_library (BUILD.bazel:105-156) has no additional_linker_inputs, data, or extra_srcs for this file, and there is no corresponding install rule. MSVC consumers will lose IDE natvis pretty-printing for nlohmann::json objects.

findings.summary: nlohmann_json.pc hardcodes /usr/local/include rather than deriving from the install prefix
findings.evidence: The CMake configure_file step for pkg-config.pc.in (CMakeLists.txt:141-144) substitutes CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR which tracks the actual install prefix. The Bazel write_file gen_nlohmann_json_pc (BUILD.bazel:21-38) hardcodes 'Cflags: -I/usr/local/include' regardless of where the package is actually installed; any non-default prefix (e.g. /opt/local, /usr) produces a broken pc file.
